edges.source: Low Neonatal Renal Mineralocorticoid Receptor Expression

edges.description: Reproduces neonatal renal salt wasting with compensatory renin-aldosterone activation.
edges.limitations: The model is homozygous null and lethal, whereas the human disease is heterozygous and usually remits with salt. It therefore models complete MR loss rather than the haploinsufficiency that causes PHA1A.

nodes.description: Volume contraction and the failed MR response drive renin, angiotensin II and aldosterone up. Aldosterone falls with age but stays high for life, making it a marker for asymptomatic carriers. In adults the compensation is accompanied by increased salt appetite.

evidence.reference_title: Renin-aldosterone system evaluation over four decades in an extended family with autosomal dominant pseudohypoaldosteronism due to a deletion in the NR3C2 gene.
evidence.snippet: The long-term follow-up showed an age-dependent decrease in both plasma renin activity and serum aldosterone levels over the years. However, aldosterone levels remain high life-long.

evidence.reference_title: Renal pseudohypoaldosteronism type 1
evidence.snippet: Typical presentation is in the neonatal period with weight loss, failure to thrive, vomiting and dehydration in association with hyponatremia, hyperkalemia and metabolic acidosis as well as elevated aldosterone and renin levels.

nodes.description: Renal salt and water loss contracts the extracellular volume, producing dehydration, weight loss and, in severe cases, hypotension and death in the neonatal period.

evidence.reference_title: Renal pseudohypoaldosteronism type 1-an adult case series including a novel gene variant.
evidence.snippet: Symptoms are failure to thrive, vomiting, and weight loss.

evidence.reference_title: NR3C2 / autosomal dominant pseudohypoaldosteronism type 1 (Definitive)
evidence.snippet: This disorder is characterised by mineralocorticoid resistance and neonatal renal salt wasting, and failure to thrive in neonates and children.

nodes.description: Can be severe enough in infancy to cause electrocardiographic changes.

nodes.description: MR contributes to negative feedback on the HPA axis. Adults with NR3C2 haploinsufficiency have higher morning cortisol and cortisol metabolite excretion than unaffected relatives, which in a small study was associated with lower HDL cholesterol and higher waist circumference.

evidence.reference_title: Activation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis in adults with mineralocorticoid receptor haploinsufficiency.
evidence.snippet: Patients with PHA1 had higher morning plasma cortisol (816 ± 85 vs 586 ± 50 nmol/L, P = .02) and increased 24-hour urinary excretion of cortisol metabolites (985 ± 150 vs 640 ± 46 μg/mmol creatinine, P = .03), independently of gender.

nodes.description: Aldosterone-stimulated sodium reabsorption in the distal nephron fails, so the kidney loses sodium and water. In MR-null mice, fractional sodium excretion rose more than 8-fold with normal glomerular filtration and reduced but persistent ENaC-mediated reabsorption.

nodes.description: Healthy newborns have physiologically low renal MR expression despite high aldosterone, and expression rises after birth. This developmental window is the proposed reason that loss of one NR3C2 copy causes salt wasting in early infancy but is compensated later.

evidence.reference_title: Low renal mineralocorticoid receptor expression at birth contributes to partial aldosterone resistance in neonates.
evidence.snippet: Our study provides the first evidence for a low renal MR expression level at birth, despite high aldosterone levels, which could account for compromised postnatal sodium handling.

nodes.description: MR-null mice develop normally before birth, then in the first week develop hyperkalemia, hyponatremia, very high renin, angiotensin II and aldosterone, and die around day 10 from renal sodium and water loss.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical features and molecular basis of pseudohypoaldosteronism type 1.
evidence.snippet: Mutations are found in all exons and there is no mutation hot spot. Nonsense and frameshift mutations leading to premature stop codon are the most frequent.

evidence.reference_title: NR3C2 microdeletions-an underrecognized cause of pseudohypoaldosteronism type 1A: a case report and literature review.
evidence.snippet: Sequencing (Sanger or short-read next-generation) failed to detect microdeletions in 100% of tested individuals (n = 38).

nodes.description: Heterozygous truncating, splice-site, deletion and missense NR3C2 variants remove or inactivate one copy of the mineralocorticoid receptor. Mutant receptors fail to bind aldosterone, to translocate to the nucleus or to activate transcription, or are rapidly degraded. Most tested mutants have no dominant-negative effect, so the disease is attributed to reduced receptor dosage.

nodes.description: With reduced MR dosage, principal cells of the aldosterone-sensitive distal nephron and collecting duct respond poorly to aldosterone. The resistance is limited to the kidney, unlike the systemic resistance of ENaC-related PHA1.

nodes.description: Oral (or initially intravenous) sodium chloride replaces renal sodium losses and corrects the electrolyte disturbance. Requirements fall with age and supplementation can usually be stopped in early childhood. Starting salt from day 1 after a prenatal molecular diagnosis prevented the salt-wasting presentation in one infant.
